technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Framework 6.0 baseline with Java 17+ for all development.
Leverage existing Spring Cloud Data Flow (SCDF) codebase for U1, U2, U6, U7; Spring Cloud Stream for U5; Spring Cloud Stream Kafka binder for U3.
For U1 and U2, extend SCDF REST API and UI (Angular/TypeScript) to support composed job progress aggregation and restart.
For U3, perform a spike using Kafka 0.9 client library to assess compatibility with Spring Cloud Stream binder; no production code required.
For U4, conduct a research spike on Lattice (now deprecated, but assume evaluation of container orchestration for bare metal); produce documentation only.
For U5, enhance the stream definition parser in Spring Cloud Stream to support dot-delimited property access for Tuple and JSON payloads.
For U6, implement tab completion in the SCDF shell (Spring Shell/JLine) by adding completion providers for module names and options.
For U7, create Mesos deployment artifacts (Marathon JSON templates, SCDF server Mesos profile) and integration tests using a local Mesos cluster (e.g., via Vagrant or Docker).
For U8, extract the Redis JUnit @Rule into a separate Maven module, publish to a separate Git repository and Maven repository, and update dependent projects.
assumptions: The developer has full access to the relevant Spring project repositories (SCDF, Spring Cloud Stream, etc.) and can make changes directly.
All necessary dependencies (Kafka 0.9, Lattice, Mesos) are available and compatible with Spring Framework 6.0 and Java 17.
Each user story is independent and can be implemented sequentially by a single developer; no parallel work is considered.
Unit tests, integration tests, and documentation updates are included in the estimates for each feature.
Code review and merge overhead is included in the implementation estimates (approx. 10-15% of coding time).
The existing codebases are well-structured and changes are localized to a few modules per user story.
For U3 and U4, only investigation and documentation are required; no production implementation is needed.
A local development environment with Docker, Vagrant, and a Mesos cluster simulator is available for U7 testing.
The separate repository for U8 will be hosted on GitHub and published to Maven Central via Sonatype.
